assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_live at creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt. Integrity follows from the matching cited digest for [5884,6024) and the same scoped whole-file digest on publisher_pin. Relevance follows from section 4(a) naming both trademark and patent rights. Interpretation turns on “held by Affirmer” and “licensed or otherwise affected”, alongside the express waiver verbs. Applicability follows from the Statement of Purpose defining the Affirmer as the person associating CC0 with a Work. On contradiction, sections 2 and 3 reach the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights, section 1(iv) expressly subjects unfair competition to 4(a), and section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for clearing rights of others.

challenge.method: Tested section 2's broad waiver and section 3's fallback license separately against section 4(a). Checked section 1(iv) for overlapping unfair-competition rights and section 4(c) for the treatment of other rights holders.
challenge.results: Section 2 reaches the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights, subject to applicable law. Section 3 licenses that same class to the extent the waiver is judged ineffective, and its residual nonassertion language stays within that class. Section 4(a) expressly excludes both waiver and licensing of the Affirmer's patents and trademarks. Section 1(iv) defers to 4(a), and section 4(c) leaves clearance of other persons' rights outstanding.

limitations: This finding concerns the instrument's stated effect on rights held by the Affirmer. Ownership, separate grants, defenses and clearance of third-party rights require separate evidence.
reasoning: When an Affirmer applies CC0 to a Work, section 4(a) expressly preserves the patent and trademark rights held by that Affirmer. It covers surrender under the waiver, licensing under the fallback, and any other effect of the document on those rights.
